title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (March 2027) — the control edition: the second revision of the 2028 lines, published inside the March FOMC blackout
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes) by the eia-steo-2027-02-09 never-assessed initial research and read from the RAW HTML table, whose 2027 row is "March 2027 | 03/09/2027" with a blank Notes cell; the same page states the release window as 12:00 pm-12:15 pm ET. Reproduces independently from the page's own rule ("the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", a Federal holiday on the preceding Monday pushing the release to Wednesday): 2027-03-04 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 03-09, and 2027-03-08 is a Monday that is not a Federal holiday. Filed estimate on the standing EIA grounds — this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA, and a discovering lane never self-confirms an event it found in-sweep — not on date doubt
notes: Discovered during eia-steo-2027-02-09's never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), off the same raw EIA release-schedule table that dates the February edition. Proposed for one specific reason rather than calendar completeness — it is the CONTROL for that session's central measured finding, and without it the finding cannot be scored. The February edition is the year's first published revision table (the January edition carries no "Notable forecast changes" section at all, verified absent in archives/jan25.pdf and archives/jan26.pdf and present in nine other sampled editions), so 02-09 states which direction the newly-rolled 2028 lines moved. The measured claim registered on 02-09 is that this first revision is SMALL and PROPORTIONALLY SMALLER than a mature out-year revision: on the 2026 series, February's out-year/near-year revision-magnitude ratio was 0.49 against 0.65 in March 2026 and 0.70 in August 2026, and the out-year electricity-consumption line moved +0.18% (2026) and -0.31% (2025). MARCH IS THE FIRST ORDINARY REVISION — the first month whose "previous forecast" column is itself a revised forecast rather than a first print — so 03-09's Notable-forecast-changes table is the reading that either confirms the newly-printed out-year is sticky or shows February was merely quiet. The corridor also differs from its two predecessors in a way worth its own row: per the Fed primary (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09, "Last Update: August 19, 2026") the March 16-17 2027 meeting carries a SEP asterisk, so its blackout opens Saturday 2027-03-06 and this edition publishes INSIDE the blackout and seven days before a projections meeting — where 2027-01-12 published four days before a blackout opened and 2027-02-09 publishes in no blackout at all. Three consecutive STEO days spanning three distinct blackout positions is the cleanest natural experiment this calendar has for the STEO-day null. Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning: a forecast publication sets no policy and moves no equity tape, and the measured tape agrees (pooled STEO-day median |move| n=24 is below the all-days median in every symbol tested but CRWV). The remaining 2027 STEO dates on the same table (04/06, 05/11, 06/08, 07/07, 08/10, 09/08, 11/09, 12/07; 10/13 is already tracked) are deliberately NOT proposed here — the chain proposes the next edition when it has a research question, not the whole year at once.
